newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope asks Catholics for prayers before operation.
newsitem.headline: Pope asks Catholics for prayers before operation.

text.p: Pope John Paul asked the world's Roman Catholics to pray for him on Sunday hours before he was to enter hospital for an appendix operation.

"Tonight, I will enter hospital to undergo an operation," he told tens of thousands of people in St Peter's Square. "In asking you to accompany me with your prayer, I send cordial greetings to those in hospitals and clinics, knowing I can count on their spiritual solidarity."
"May the caring Virgin Mary watch over all of us...," he added in an address at the end of a beatification ceremony that was his last public ceremony before the surgery.
The 76-year-old Pope is due to enter Rome's Gemelli hospital on Sunday night for the operation. It is likely to take place on Tuesday.

The Vatican said last month that periodic inflammation of the appendix was the cause of three bouts of "intestinal fever" which have struck the leader of the world's 960 million Roman Catholics since Christmas.

A number of doctors in Italy and abroad who are not involved in treating the Pope have expressed scepticism about the official version. The Vatican has denied Italian media reports that the Pope may be suffering from a second colon tumour following removal of a first one in 1992.
